newsitem.title: DENMARK: French Paribas lowers Danish bonds recommendation.
newsitem.headline: French Paribas lowers Danish bonds recommendation.

text.p: French bank Paribas lowered its recommendation on Monday for Danish bonds because their 10-year yield gap to Germany had likely bottomed and fears are fading for a delayed European economic and monetary union (EMU).
"We advise holders of Danish bonds to move allocation to neutral as further spread narrowing below 45-50 basis points to Germany is not expected," Paribas said in its latest bond survey.
"As fears of EMU being delayed are scaled back, Danish bonds lose their attractiveness as hedging instruments," it said.
"At the same time, investors feel that further convergence may be capped by the opt-out option, which leaves spreads in Denmark vulnerable to currency risk," Paribas said.

Denmark voted in favour of the Maastricht Treaty in a referendum in 1993, after the government reached opt-out agreements with Brussels on joint defence policy, participation in the European single currency and police and immigration cooperation.
The 10-year yield gap between Denmark's seven-percent benchmark bond due 2007 and the equivalent German bund closed at 50 basis points on Monday.
